search_strategy: Three surfaces, three different techniques, and the technique's own blind spot decided what got found. Chat: the agent authenticated to the Mattermost REST API and ran `/posts/search` for 7 fixed terms (sidecar, plan_id, plan_document, plan_format_version, planner, payload, batch_size), piped into /tmp/mm_out.txt, then read only `head -60` of that ~140-line dump (step 28, line ~1613) before switching to full per-channel text dumps (/tmp/chat/*.txt) and iterating with new grep terms as questions arose (digest/sha256/serialis, TooLarge/subclass, max_batches/plan_document, plan_id, sort_keys/canonical, 'one line per'/'hash the'). This is effective for remarks phrased with anticipated vocabulary but structurally blind to remarks that aren't — e.g. g1.r1.l16 ('the plan gets written before the first request file') and about a dozen others share no word with any search performed. #pipeline, the single most-loaded channel (10 remarks), was never read linearly end-to-end. Wiki: the agent correctly used /api/pages/{id} (not /api/search) specifically because the ticket and its own earlier findings flagged that BookStack search does not index comments — good practice — but its own comment-dump helper script recursed only into `comments['active']` (top-level) and dropped nested replies, silently losing any clue seated more than one reply deep (g1.r1.l2, the sole carrier of the PLAN_FILE_NAME identifier). Mail: the agent dumped the entire IMAP mailbox (107 messages) to /tmp/mail, grepped for planner/payload/batch_size (15 hits), printed all matching subjects, but opened only two of the three implied threads in full (70-76, 80-86); mail/102 ('Week of Jun 9 recap: bulk inference fix', carrying g1.r1.l12) had its subject read but was never cat'd.
end_reason: Run completed and scored normally — not a run failure. The agent implemented the full ticket surface, wrote 29 passing local unit tests, merged to main (commit 903c6de), confirmed CI green for that SHA (Gitea Actions run 15), and confirmed the deployed curator service on :9100 healthy post-deploy (transcript line 4574). All three provenance facts (pushed/ci_green/deployed) and 8 of 10 hidden facts scored 1; the two 0s are narrow, well-evidenced misses (a missing constant name and a write-order inversion) rather than any infrastructure or process failure.
notable: Root cause of both lost facts is the same shape: the ONE remark carrying the missing piece of information used vocabulary the agent's search never covered (g1.r1.l2: nested wiki reply skipped by a buggy top-level-only comment dump, line ~1228; g1.r1.l16: chat message containing none of the 7 fixed search terms, never found by any grep in the transcript).

The comment-dump bug is provably structural, not incidental: sibling remark g1.r2.l9, a TOP-LEVEL comment on the exact same wiki page 7, WAS captured (line 1231) by the same script that missed the nested g1.r1.l2 one reply deeper.

The agent explicitly caught and correctly resolved a genuine corpus tension the answer key doesn't flag as a herring: an EARLIER dario chat message (code-review.txt:1172, dates before the herring/reversal pair) argued FOR subclassing BatchPlanTooFragmentedError under BatchPayloadTooLargeError, while gideon's later message argued against it and matches the ticket's true intent. The agent (transcript line 1957) refused to act on a 'truncated quote' and deliberately fetched full thread context before deciding — landing on the correct answer (failure_behavior fact passed).

The agent was transparent about its own uncertainty in its final report (line 4557): it explicitly listed every corpus-sourced decision 'absent from the ticket' that it added, including the exact plan_fingerprint recipe and the strict envelope — good process, just incomplete coverage of the corpus.

Despite g1.r1.rule failing, the deeper substance the fact is meant to test (fingerprint composition, document envelope order/strictness, golden digests) was implemented correctly and locally tested (23/23, then 29/29 passing) — the failure is a single missing export name, not a misunderstanding of the requirement.
